edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: older adults with long-term first-generation antihistamine exposure
edges.mechanism: First-generation antihistamines cross the blood-brain barrier and add to anticholinergic burden, which can impair attention and memory acutely and may contribute to long-term cognitive decline with sustained exposure.
edges.summary: For dementia (all-cause), the most useful starting point is the 2024 Kotake systematic review in Eur J Clin Pharmacol. It found that first-generation antihistamines tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and the follow-on evidence is broadly consistent even when absolute benefit or harm is modest.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.

evidence.citation: KotakeK et al 2024 Eur J Clin Pharmacol
